introduction: This foundational level explores the most basic units of the legal system. It breaks down the anatomy of a 'Legal Right' according to Salmond, defines the absolute power of 'Ownership', and introduces the physical reality of 'Possession'.

core_concepts.title: What is a Legal Right? (Salmond's 5 Elements)
core_concepts.description:
According to Sir John Salmond, a legal right is an 'interest recognized and protected by a rule of legal justice'. Every valid legal right MUST possess 5 essential elements:
1. Person of Inherence (Subject): The person who owns the right.
2. Person of Incidence: The person upon whom the corresponding duty lies.
3. Content (Act/Forbearance): The specific act the person of incidence is bound to do or not do.
4. Object (Subject-matter): The thing over which the right is exercised (e.g., a car, a reputation).
5. Title: The facts or events by which the right became vested in its owner (e.g., a sale deed).

core_concepts.title: Ownership: The Ultimate Right
core_concepts.description:
Ownership is the absolute and ultimate right a person can have over an object. 
- John Austin's Definition: Ownership is a right over a determinate thing which is (1) Indefinite in point of user (you can use it however you want), (2) Unrestricted in point of disposition (you can sell/gift it to anyone), and (3) Unlimited in point of duration (it lasts forever/until you die).
- Note: In modern times, ownership is NEVER truly absolute (e.g., the State can acquire your land, or restrict you from building a chemical plant on it).

core_concepts.title: Possession: Nine-Tenths of the Law
core_concepts.description:
While Ownership is a strictly *legal* concept (a right), Possession is a *factual/physical* concept. It is the continuing exercise of a claim to the exclusive use of a material object.
Law protects possession because maintaining peace requires that physical control over things shouldn't be violently disturbed, even if the possessor isn't the true owner. (Hence, 'Possession is nine-tenths of the law').

core_concepts.title: The 2 Elements of Possession
core_concepts.description:
To legally 'possess' something, two elements must coexist:
1. Corpus Possessionis: The objective element. The actual physical control over the object.
2. Animus Possidendi: The subjective element. The mental intention to exclude others from interfering with the object.

important_entities.name: Corpus without Animus
important_entities.key_fact: Physical control without intent is NOT possession.
important_entities.significance: If you hold your friend's bag for 5 minutes while they tie their shoe, you have *Corpus* (physical control) but no *Animus* (intent to exclude others or own it). Legally, you do not have 'Possession'; you merely have 'Custody'.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners will ask: 'A promises to give B a gift for his birthday but fails to do so. Does B have a legal right?' **NO**. A legal right must be recognized AND protected by the State. A moral right or social expectation without State sanction is legally meaningless.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: S I C O T (Subject, Incidence, Content, Object, Title)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Use SICOT to remember the exact anatomy of every legal right.

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever a Judiciary question asks 'Which jurist defined ownership as indefinite in user, unrestricted in disposition, and unlimited in duration?', select **John Austin**.
